title: Four-goal Switch
story: Each team attacks two doors, so the best route can switch whenever defenders close one side.
setup: Create a 20x25-yard field with two mini goals on each end line. Play 2v2 or 3v3 and keep spare balls beside both touchlines.
instructions: Each team attacks the two goals on the opposite end line and defends its own two.
Play freely for three-minute rounds with rapid restarts from the coach or nearest player.
Rotate teams and any goalkeeper turns between rounds; avoid fixed positions.
Ask one short question between rounds, then let the game teach.
coach_lens: Observe players looking away from a crowded goal, spreading naturally and reacting when possession changes. Do not add pass-count or touch restrictions.
questions: If one door is crowded, what else can you see?
What changes the moment your team wins the ball?

simplify: Widen the field or goals and play 3v2 temporarily.
challenge: Narrow the field slightly before adding any rule.
low_attendance: Play 2v2 or 3v2 and rotate the extra attacker every round.
high_attendance: Create a second field so games remain 2v2 or 3v3.
limited_equipment: Use cone gates; if only two goals exist, place one goal and one cone gate at each end.

safety: Leave retrieval space behind every goal and keep spectators clear.
Use spare balls only after the previous ball is safely out.

diagram.alt: A three-versus-three game has two goals at each end; arrows show the attacking direction switching toward the less crowded goal.

source.title: Trainingspraxis: 3 gegen 3 im Funino-Feld
source.reviewer_notes: Adapted from the DFB four-mini-goal small-sided format and its joy, intensity and repetition principles. SmallSide supplies original English delivery, adaptations, safety language and artwork.
